author: Russell Brand
description:
Two working-class men in Ireland, people who would benefit from the exact same political liberties and protections, are caught on camera pulling weapons on each other in the street, and Russell Brand uses the footage to make one of his most urgent points yet. The economic systems that promised ordinary people participation in the middle class are collapsing, the material carrots used to keep people incentivized and divided are disappearing, and the frustration has nowhere to go except sideways at the people right next to you. Russell argues that once working-class people on both sides of the political divide recognize they are fighting the same enemy from below, the alliance that forms will be something the establishment has no answer for.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand makes the case that doomscrolling is not a cause but a symptom — the expression of a deep spiritual malady in a culture that has stripped sanctity from life, told people they are meaningless, and then acted surprised when they cannot stop staring at their phones. The UK government's response, he argues, is predictably revealing: overnight curfews on social media for teenagers, VPN restrictions, AI chatbot controls, and a quiet push to redefine what social media even is — not to help anyone but to justify another layer of censorship and control. Once you understand that the emptiness driving the addiction was created by the same system now offering to fix it, the whole thing becomes a lot clearer.
